title: Perfume brand (one fragrance)

fields.label: What it smells like
fields.help: The notes from first spray to drydown, in your own words.

fields.label: Type and strength
fields.help: e.g. eau de parfum, about 18%, lasts 7-9 hours

fields.label: Anything else
fields.help: Batch sizes, where it's made, free samples, refills...

writerNotes: The hero is a fixed animation: a glass bottle fills, then scrolling is time on skin. The liquid changes colour through exactly nine notes, three top, three heart, three base, in the order of notes[0..8]. Each note's colour is the liquid colour at that moment: pick a colour that evokes the note (#rrggbb, mid to light, readable on a dark room).

timeline gives the minutes when the heart and base notes take over and when the scent ends; match the brief's longevity. tiers[].range and hud.end.phase / hud.end.clock describe the same times in words.
notes[].share is each note's share of the formula in percent; the nine shares must add up to 100.
product.name may put one word in *italics* (the original is 'Fig *Hour*'). product.concentrationType is cologne, toilette, parfum or extrait, and product.concentration must sit inside its range.
pulse is five pulse points in fixed positions on a body drawing: ears, throat, inner elbow, wrist, scarf - keep those places, rewrite the advice.
quiz.results are three results (green/top, powder/heart, smoke/base in the original): rewrite them for this scent's top, heart and base. quiz.where is three spraying plans from light to strong.
sizes.items are three bottle sizes, smallest first; the middle one is the one the page features. Prices are whole numbers.

specs are six facts about the fragrance (concentration, longevity, sillage, one spray, maceration, where made). Use only facts from the brief; for anything the brief doesn't say, keep a neutral version of the example's wording and list the path in _assumed.
theme.wordmarkFit: always "fit", and leave out theme.captionFit, for a new business (the example sets "crop" and "off" only to reproduce the original exactly).

business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed. Where space is tight the design uses business.short: a short form of the same name that the business would recognise (e.g. drop Ltd, Studio or & Co), never a different name.

product.name is set to exactly the fragrance name in the brief; you may only add *italics* to one word. product.short is the form for the HUD and the bottle label: the same name, or a recognisable shortening of it (e.g. "No. 9" for "Barbershop No. 9"), never a new name.
